# Atlas Data API (EOL) — concept pack

> Source-anchored research for Atlas Data API (EOL). Run status: COMPLETED.

## Vocabulary

Terms this pack was harvested with, grouped by their relation to the concept; counts are units matched / sources. Zero-hit terms are listed under Coverage. On every unit line, `keywords:` names the terms that matched.

- **self**: Atlas Data API (EOL) (16/4)

## How it works

- [statement] MongoDB's App Services Admin API notice states that database triggers remain available despite Data API EOL. The notice also says the retirement affects authentication, user management, functions, Wire Protocol, and data access permissions; it does not support treating every App Services capability as unaffected. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-09-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-app-services-admin-api-v3 · keywords: Atlas Data API (EOL)
- [statement] The Data API EOL should not be generalized to every App Services capability: MongoDB's EOL notice explicitly says database triggers remain available. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-app-services-admin-api-v3 · keywords: Atlas Data API (EOL)

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Retained Data API configuration endpoints in the App Services Admin API are explicitly marked deprecated. Their continued appearance in an API reference does not establish that an application can enable or use Data API after EOL. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-app-services-admin-api-v3 · keywords: Atlas Data API (EOL) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-app-services-admin-api-v3/group/endpoint-data-api
- [statement] The surviving Data API v1 reference still describes setup and authentication, but labels the API deprecated and gives June 12, 2025 as its last update. Read alongside MongoDB's explicit EOL notice, these instructions do not establish present service availability. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-data-api-v1 · keywords: Atlas Data API (EOL) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-app-services-admin-api-v3

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Atlas Data API reached end of life on September 30, 2025; it is a retired dependency rather than a service with a future deprecation deadline. MongoDB states the EOL date, and RESTHeart independently markets migration from the removed service. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-app-services-admin-api-v3 · keywords: Atlas Data API (EOL) · also: https://restheart.com/mongo-data-api-replacement/
- [statement] FerretDB's documented Data API is integrated into FerretDB, a PostgreSQL-backed MongoDB-compatible database. It is a route to a different database architecture, rather than merely adding an HTTP proxy in front of an existing Atlas cluster. (high confidence) — https://docs.ferretdb.io/usage/data-api/ · keywords: Atlas Data API (EOL) · also: https://blog.ferretdb.io/best-alternative-to-mongodb-data-api-and-http-endpoints/, https://blog.dreamfactory.com/the-best-atlas-data-api-alternatives-in-2026-a-complete-comparison
- [statement] FerretDB v2.7 documents its Data API as an integrated FerretDB feature rather than a standalone service. It exposes HTTP MongoDB-compatible operations and is enabled with FERRETDB_LISTEN_DATA_API_ADDR or --listen-data-api-addr. Its examples use /action/findOne and HTTP Basic credentials. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-02-07) — https://docs.ferretdb.io/usage/data-api/ · keywords: Atlas Data API (EOL)

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The former Data API exposed application-data reads, writes, and aggregations through HTTP. Its retained v1 specification lists find, insert, update, delete, and aggregate actions; it was powered by Atlas Functions and used application authentication and role-based permissions. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-data-api-v1 · keywords: Atlas Data API (EOL) · also: https://modelence.com/blog/migrate-mongodb-data-api
- [statement] The former global v1 base URL was https://data.mongodb-api.com/app/{ClientAppID}/endpoint/data/v1. The administrative reference also documents regional base URLs for locally deployed apps. These are historical identification patterns for dependency inventories. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-data-api-v1 · keywords: Atlas Data API (EOL) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-app-services-admin-api-v3/group/endpoint-data-api
- [statement] MongoDB distinguishes the App Services Admin API, which configures and deploys applications, from the app-specific HTTPS APIs used by client applications. Treating the old Data API base URL as an administrative API confuses these two roles. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-app-services-admin-api-v3 · keywords: Atlas Data API (EOL) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-data-api-v1
- [statement] In its February 28, 2025 walkthrough, FerretDB demonstrates insert, find, update, and delete over action endpoints. Its documentation also shows those actions using HTTP Basic credentials and an explicitly enabled Data API listener, so migration includes endpoint and authentication configuration. (medium confidence) — https://docs.ferretdb.io/usage/data-api/ · keywords: Atlas Data API (EOL) · also: https://blog.ferretdb.io/best-alternative-to-mongodb-data-api-and-http-endpoints/
- [statement] Modelence's August 13, 2026 migration guide describes configuring a MongoDB URI and a Data API key, exchanging the key at /auth/providers/api-key/login, and sending the returned bearer token to /data/v1/action/insertOne. This is the provider's documented workflow, not a tested assertion of complete Atlas compatibility. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-13) — https://modelence.com/blog/migrate-mongodb-data-api · keywords: Atlas Data API (EOL)
- [statement] RESTHeart markets an Atlas Data API-compatible migration service. Its landing page establishes that the provider offers this route, but does not document an exhaustive compatibility matrix or prove that changing only the hostname preserves all application behavior. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-14) — https://restheart.com/mongo-data-api-replacement/ · keywords: Atlas Data API (EOL)
- [statement] Historically, Atlas Data API exposed document reads, writes, and aggregation through app-specific HTTPS endpoints. The App Services Admin API instead configured applications and their API surfaces; it was not the client application's document-operation interface. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-data-api-v1 · keywords: Atlas Data API (EOL) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-app-services-admin-api-v3
- [statement] Migration review should cover authentication and data-access permissions as well as endpoint URLs. The historical Data API depended on App Services authentication and role-based permissions, and MongoDB's EOL notice explicitly lists authentication, user management, and data-access permissions among impacted capabilities. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-data-api-v1 · keywords: Atlas Data API (EOL) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-app-services-admin-api-v3
- [statement] Do not assume that an HTTP replacement preserves the original authentication contract: MongoDB's historical reference describes App Services login credentials or session access tokens, whereas FerretDB's v2.7 request examples use Basic authentication. Validate credentials and authorization during migration. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-data-api-v1 · keywords: Atlas Data API (EOL) · also: https://docs.ferretdb.io/usage/data-api/
